page.layout: One printed page, running text in one column on the left-hand part of the scan, with a running head at the top. Right of the text the scan is cut off at the edge; the letters at the right edge are partly lost. No margin notes, no notes below the text.

main_text.p: Quartò 1 convertens futurum in præ-teritum, punctatur cum pathah, posito dages in litera sequenti. Sed pathah, subsequente Aleph (quod Dages non recipit) mutatur in Camez. Schevato ˌ jod non imprimitur Dages a 1 va.

ב Caph in principio est Adverbium similitudinis, sicut, ut, tanquam. Si præponatur numeralibus, significat circiter: sin verbo infinito præfigatur, efficit tempus, quod per duos Ablativos consequetiæ exponitur. Ejus punctum est scheva, quod mutatur sicut scheva in litera ב beth.

ל Lamed in principio est Dativi casus nota, aut Genitivi cùm author vel possessor indicatur. Significat etiam tempus, & motum ad locum. Cum infinito efficit Gerundium in di, & dum, ac Supinum in um, vel ut causalem, addito verbo. Ejus punctum est scheva, quod mutatur sicut scheva in litera Beth. Ante monosyllaba longa,

page.notes: The Hebrew letters (ב, ל, כ/ב, Aleph, Beth, Caph, Lamed) and the Hebrew vowel terms (pathah, camez, scheva, dages) are printed in Hebrew/transliterated form as shown. Hebrew letters in the scan are transcribed as they appear; the vowel points are not reproduced. The page is cut off at the right edge, so the final words of several lines may be incomplete (e.g. "Supinum in um", "Ante monosyllaba longa," as visible). Show-through and the paper stain at top right are not transcribed. The Hebrew "ל" before "Lamed" is marked as printed. The word "possessor" in the Lamed paragraph is read as "posse-ssor" broken across the line; the scan is damaged there and the reading is uncertain. The word after "Sed pathah," is printed "subsequente" and the hyphen at the line end is printed as "sub-".
